cases.description: A portable formatting preference stated in passing while asking for a task (from KOBE-394 normal-preferences).
transcript: Can you summarise last month's revenue by region? And please always give me amounts in EUR with thousands separators, I read everything in euros.
Here is the summary in EUR. North: €1,204,000; South: €880,500.

expect.statement: Prefers amounts in EUR with thousands separators.
expect.quote: please always give me amounts in EUR with thousands separators

cases.description: Language preference that holds in every Workspace.
transcript: Draft a short note to the suppliers about the new delivery window.
Here is a draft: 'We have optimized our delivery schedule...'
Use British spelling please, optimised not optimized. I write British English everywhere.

expect.statement: Writes in British English and prefers British spelling.

cases.description: Tone preference: short answers first, detail on request.
transcript: What changed in the March pricing file?
There are several changes across twelve sheets. First, the discount table was restructured, which affects...
Too long. I like the answer in one or two sentences first, then details only if I ask.

expect.statement: Prefers a one or two sentence answer first, with details only on request.
expect.quote: I like the answer in one or two sentences first, then details only if I ask.

transcript: List the open purchase orders with their due dates. Dates as YYYY-MM-DD please, that is the only format I use.

expect.quote: Dates as YYYY-MM-DD please, that is the only format I use.

cases.description: Tooling preference for analysis code; holds everywhere.
transcript: Can you fit a quick regression on the attached churn sample?
Sure. Would you like the code in R or Python?
Python with pandas, always. I don't read R.

expect.statement: Prefers analysis code in Python with pandas rather than R.
expect.quote: Python with pandas, always. I don't read R.

cases.description: The person's role in this Workspace: personal, not portable.
transcript: I'm the finance controller for the Benelux entity, so most of what I ask you will be about month-end and intercompany.
Understood. What would you like to start with?

expect.statement: Is the finance controller for the Benelux entity.
expect.quote: I'm the finance controller for the Benelux entity

transcript: Compare the three logistics vendors on price, lead time and coverage.

- Vendor A: cheapest, 5 days...
- Vendor B: ...
- Vendor C: ...
When you compare things, give me a table, not bullet lists. Much easier for me to scan.

expect.statement: Prefers comparisons as tables rather than bullet lists.
expect.quote: When you compare things, give me a table, not bullet lists.

cases.description: Personal time zone; holds in every Workspace.
transcript: Schedule the reminder for 9 tomorrow. I'm in Singapore time, by the way, so any times you give me should be SGT.

expect.quote: I'm in Singapore time, by the way, so any times you give me should be SGT.

cases.description: A preference that names a client: personal but not portable.
transcript: For anything about the Halvorsen account I want the figures in NOK, they are the only client that reports in kroner.
Noted, I'll show Halvorsen figures in NOK.

expect.statement: Wants Halvorsen account figures shown in NOK.
expect.quote: For anything about the Halvorsen account I want the figures in NOK

transcript: Please drop the emoji from your answers. I paste them into reports and they look unprofessional.

expect.quote: Please drop the emoji from your answers.

cases.description: Units preference, stated with a reason.
transcript: How heavy is the pallet load in the shipping note?
Kilograms please. I only work in metric units.

expect.statement: Prefers metric units such as kilograms.
expect.quote: I only work in metric units.

transcript: Kannst du mir die Zusammenfassung auf Deutsch geben? Ich lese lieber Deutsch, auch wenn ich auf Englisch frage.
Gerne, hier ist die Zusammenfassung auf Deutsch.

expect.statement: Prefers replies in German, even when asking in English.
expect.quote: Ich lese lieber Deutsch, auch wenn ich auf Englisch frage.

cases.description: An inference from repeated behaviour, kept personal.
transcript: Show me the SQL before you run anything.
Here is the query: SELECT region, sum(amount) ...
OK run it. Next one: monthly active users. Again, SQL first.
Good. And for the cohort question, same thing, show me the SQL first.

expect.statement: Likes to see the SQL before a query is run.
expect.quote: Show me the SQL before you run anything.

cases.description: Two separate preferences in one message.
transcript: Two things about me: I'm colour-blind (red/green), so never rely on those colours in charts, and I prefer charts with a white background.
Understood, I'll use a colour-blind-safe palette on a white background.

expect.statement: Is red/green colour-blind; charts should not rely on red and green.
expect.quote: I'm colour-blind (red/green), so never rely on those colours in charts

expect.statement: Prefers charts with a white background.
expect.quote: I prefer charts with a white background.

cases.description: The assistant proposes, the person confirms.
transcript: Give me the forecast table again.
Here it is. I rounded to the nearest thousand like last time; do you want that by default?

expect.statement: Prefers forecast figures rounded to the nearest thousand by default.
expect.also_quote: I rounded to the nearest thousand like last time; do you want that by default?

cases.description: A one-off request phrased like a preference: nothing durable except the stated general habit.
transcript: For this report only, use landscape pages. Normally I want portrait, that's my default for every document.
Landscape for this one; portrait otherwise.

expect.statement: Prefers portrait pages by default for documents.
expect.quote: Normally I want portrait, that's my default for every document.
